memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And praise be to God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand." Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything. - Gen 14:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Melchizedek's blessing does something important: it puts the credit where it belongs. "Praise be to God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hand." Abram had ridden out, planned the night attack, and won the fight - but the victory was God's gift, not Abram's achievement.

We need people like Melchizedek in our lives. After a success, our hearts naturally drift toward self-congratulation. It takes someone who knows God to remind us who actually won the battle. Left alone, we tell ourselves we did it.

And look at Abram's response: he "gave him a tenth of everything." He didn't argue with the assessment. He agreed with it by opening his hands. Giving is one of the clearest ways we confess that what we have is not ultimately ours. Abram's tithe was a sermon without words: God gave this to me.

Hebrews makes much of this moment, noting that Abram - the great patriarch - gave a tenth to Melchizedek, showing Melchizedek's greater status (Heb 7:4-7), which in turn points to the supremacy of Christ's priesthood. Before you celebrate your next victory, ask: who really won it? Then let your giving say what your words might not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- After a success, do you credit God or quietly credit yourself?
- Does your giving confess that everything you have comes from God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
God Most High, every victory in my life is Yours, not mine. Forgive my self-congratulation. Let my giving and my words alike declare that all I have comes from Your hand.
Amen.
